title: If You Own AI Stocks.. GET READY FOR A BIG CHANGE!
summary: Couch Investor recaps Snowflake's earnings (revenue +36% YoY, net revenue retention 126%, FY27 growth guide raised from 29% to 36%, annual guidance raised $230M — excellent but not cheap) and Broadcom's report ($29.5B revenue; FY28 AI semiconductor guide of $230B; AI revenue beat 4.4%, infrastructure software miss 1.6%; an Apollo/Blackstone XPU financing vehicle for 20GW of OpenAI/Anthropic compute; gross margin guided down to 73%; customer ramps at Alphabet, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta; Hock Tan's claim that custom chips beat general-purpose GPUs). He covers Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 launch with dirt-cheap per-token pricing and a data feedback loop that strengthens future models, plus Google's Gemini 3.8 flash releases and a rumored big Gemini 4. Other items: Anduril reportedly going public with $103B in contracted revenue, and a Sam Altman clip arguing data-center water use is a myth (38,000 ChatGPT queries ≈ the water in one California almond) — though the creator says CEOs must show proof, not just claims, to shift perception. His thesis: cheaper, more efficient models mean cloud players, big AI companies, and software win big, while businesses selling only LLM subscriptions face trouble; AI demand will keep flowing between players regardless of Anthropic or OpenAI outcomes. Call: GOOGL HOLD — he loves his Google position but flags the big execution gap between Gemini and what Claude/ChatGPT can do.
